taste.name: Jumps, not ladders
taste.trigger: When separating labels, titles and statements on a page with very little text
taste.decision: Chose a x2 doubling scale (13.22 -> 26.45 -> 52.90) with one intermediate over a 5-7 step 1.25x ladder
taste.reason: With so few words each one has to announce its rank instantly; sizes 25% apart read as an accident, sizes 100% apart read as a decision

taste.name: The accent belongs to the hardware
taste.trigger: When choosing where the brand orange could appear on a page selling an orange-keyed instrument
taste.decision: Chose to keep orange on the product and one label (#FF5000, 1.6% of background area) over tinting buttons, headings or nav
taste.reason: An accent spread across chrome becomes wallpaper; held back, the eye reads orange as 'this is the thing you press'

taste.name: No containers
taste.trigger: When grouping specs, captions, diagrams and photos down an 18,000px page
taste.decision: Chose full-bleed background bands and ~200px of empty field over cards, borders or drop shadows
taste.reason: Boxes make content feel like inventory to compare; bands make it a sequence you walk through, which suits one product told in scenes

taste.name: Labels vs readouts
taste.trigger: When the page had to carry both navigation and hard specifications
taste.decision: Chose a thin lowercase house face for places and an all-caps technical face for facts over one family in several weights
taste.reason: A front panel prints its labels and its display differently so a glance tells you which is which; specs read as measurements, not marketing
evidence: te-20 884 nodes, weight 100 x51 on nav
TechnoType 130 nodes on the uppercase spec list
